🧳 External / portable drive · 🗑️ Deleted files

Recover Deleted Files From an External Hard Drive

Deleting a file usually does not wipe it. It just marks its space as free, so the data stays until new files are saved over it. Check the Recycle Bin or Trash first, because many computers keep one for external drives too. If the files are not there, recovery tools are your main option.

1/5 · Safe to DIY
Success odds: High

If the drive is healthy, recovery only reads data and changes nothing, as long as you save the results to a different drive.

✋ Stop! Don't do this first

  • Stop copying, saving or editing files on this drive now. New data can overwrite your deleted files.
  • Do not install recovery software onto the affected drive. Install it on your computer's own drive.
  • Do not save recovered files back to the same drive. Pick a different drive.

Your steps

0 of 7 done
  1. Show me how
    1. Windows: click the small USB icon in the bottom-right taskbar, then Eject. Mac: drag the drive icon to the Trash, or click the eject button in Finder.
    2. Leave it idle until you are ready to scan.
    3. If it is a portable SSD (a drive with no moving parts) rather than a spinning drive, read the SSD guide too, because SSDs often erase deleted data quickly.
  2. Show me how
    1. Windows: open the Recycle Bin on the desktop and look for your files. Right-click, then Restore. Mac: click Trash in the Dock, right-click, then Put Back.
    2. Look in File History (Windows), Time Machine (Mac), or any cloud backup such as OneDrive, iCloud or Google Drive.
    3. Check other computers and phones where the files might have been copied.
  3. Show me how
    1. Use your computer's internal drive or another drive with enough free space.
    2. Windows: open File Explorer, This PC to see free space. Mac: select the drive in Finder and press Command-I.
  4. Show me how
    1. Plug it straight into a USB port on your computer, not through a hub or a dock.
    2. Leave it in its enclosure. You do not need to take the drive out.
  5. Show me how
    1. Download TestDisk from cgsecurity.org to your computer's own drive and unzip it. Windows: run testdisk_win.exe as administrator. Linux live USB: type sudo apt install testdisk, then sudo testdisk. Mac: in Terminal type brew install testdisk, then sudo testdisk.
    2. Choose Create, pick your external drive by its size, accept the partition type, then choose Advanced, pick the partition and choose Undelete.
    3. Highlight a file, press c to copy, move to a folder on your destination drive, then press C to confirm.

    Guide: How to use TestDisk to copy files off a driveGuide: Data recovery glossary for beginners

  6. Show me how
    1. Run photorec_win.exe (Windows, as administrator) or sudo photorec (Mac or Linux, installed with TestDisk as above).
    2. Pick the external drive and partition, use File Opt to tick the file types you want, then choose Free if you only want deleted files.
    3. Pick Other as the file system unless it is a Linux drive, move to a folder on your destination drive and press C to start. Wait for it to say it has finished.

    Guide: How to use PhotoRec to recover photos and files

  7. Show me how
    1. Open a sample of each file type to check it works fully.
    2. Keep the external drive untouched until you are happy with the results.
Mission complete! 🎉 Check your recovered files open properly, then back them up in two places.

Tools you'll use

TestDisk

Free open-source tool that finds lost partitions and repairs boot sectors so files can be read again.

  • Windows · macOS · Linux
  • Free (open source)

WebsiteDocs

PhotoRec

Free open-source file carver that recovers files by signature, even when the file system is damaged.

  • Windows · macOS · Linux
  • Free (open source)

WebsiteDocs

smartmontools

Free open-source suite that reads S.M.A.R.T. health data from drives to show early signs of failure.

  • Windows · macOS · Linux
  • Free (open source)

WebsiteDocs

CrystalDiskInfo

Free Windows app that shows a drive's S.M.A.R.T. health status, temperature and other key attributes.

Questions people ask

Are deleted files on an external drive in the Recycle Bin?

Often yes. Windows and macOS usually keep a Recycle Bin or Trash for external hard drives, so check there first. If they are not there, stop writing to the drive and use recovery software.

Do I need to take the drive out of its case?

No, scan it while it is still in its case. Many portables have USB built onto the drive or encrypt data through the case's board, so removing it can make the data unreadable.

Why are recovered file names missing?

PhotoRec finds files by what they contain, not by the drive's records, so names and folders are often lost. TestDisk can sometimes keep them.

Before you start: Educational DIY guide, no warranty. DIY recovery can cause permanent data loss. If the data is valuable, consider a professional first.
